title: Search a 2D Matrix
prompt:
Each row of `matrix` is sorted left-to-right, and the first element of each row is greater than the last element of the previous row. Return whether `target` is present, in O(log(m·n)).

**Example**: target `3` in `[[1,3,5,7],[10,11,16,20],[23,30,34,60]]` → `true`.

The whole matrix is one sorted sequence — binary search it, mapping a flat index back to `[mid / cols][mid % cols]`.
hints: Treat the m×n grid as one array of length m·n.
For a flat index `mid`, the real cell is `matrix[mid / cols][mid % cols]`.

solution.explanation: The row-ordering guarantee means the flattened grid is fully sorted, so a single binary search works. `mid / n` and `mid % n` convert a 1-D index to (row, col). O(log(m·n)).
